transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt lately. I'm just... tense all day, really. It's like I'm constantly waiting for something else to go wrong. And I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. It's just really weighing on me, and I need to figure out how to deal with it.
Have you experienced or witnessed a traumatic event that these feelings seem connected to?

I'm not really sure if you would call it a traumatic event, honestly. I mean... I know what I saw, and it was a really bad situation, but I don't really know how to label it. It's just... something that happened, and I just feel like I should have caught it or stopped it before it did. I don't really know if that counts as trauma, it's just what I've been dealing with.
Can you tell me exactly what happened in the situation you witnessed?

I... I don't really think I'm ready to go into the exact details of it right now, to be honest. It's just hard to talk about. 

It was a situation at work, at a site I was at, and things just went really wrong. I just don't really want to spell out exactly what I saw just yet, if that's okay. I just know I was there, and I feel like I should have caught whatever caused it.
Since the event, have unwanted memories of what happened been coming back to you repeatedly, such as through intrusive thoughts, nightmares, or flashbacks?

Yes, they do come back. It happens during the day mostly. I'll just be at work, measuring a railing or... or I'll just hear a ladder scrape against a wall, and out of nowhere, I just see him falling. It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops completely, and my hands start shaking so bad I have to put my clipboard down. It just hits me out of nowhere.
How long has it been since the event happened?

It's been about four months. The site I mentioned earlier... it was actually a porch repair. And the person I saw fall, it was my husband. So, yeah, this has all been going on for about four months, ever since his fall.
Since your husband’s fall, have you been deliberately avoiding places, activities, conversations, or anything else that reminds you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. At work, I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. I just pass them on to someone else. And at home... I find excuses not to talk about the repair at all. I even avoid looking at the exact spot where it happened. I just try to keep my distance from it as much as I can.
Since the fall, have you been more easily startled than you were before?
No, not really. I mean, I guess I jump a little if someone drops something heavy right behind me, but... no more than anyone else would. I haven't noticed being extra jumpy or anything like that.
Since your husband’s fall, have you been having difficulty sleeping?

Yeah, I definitely have. Most nights, I just lie there replaying things for an hour or two before I can even drift off. And then, even when I do fall asleep, I end up waking up at every little creak in the house. Or I wake up from these dreams where I... I hear him hit the ground again. So, sleep has been pretty tough.
